chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', who said:
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about al-sa'ibah. He said:

It is a man who frees his غلام, then says to him: 'Go wherever you wish. I have no share in your inheritance, nor am I liable for any offense on your behalf,' and he has two witnesses testify to that.

key_terms.جَرِيرَتِكَ: your liability or offense for which responsibility might be claimed
key_terms.ٱلسَّائِبَةِ: a freed person left unattached by the former master under a stated legal arrangement

ai.seo_question: What does al-sa'ibah mean in Shia hadith, and how is it established legally?
ai.summary: This hadith defines al-sa'ibah as a case in which a man frees his slave and formally renounces claims connected to inheritance and liability. The Imam عليه السلام explains the legal form of this arrangement and states that it is established by the testimony of two witnesses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3502 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', who said:
Abu Abdullah (as), was asked about al-sa'ibah (a freed slave who is left without ties).
Imam (as) said: "He is a man who frees his slave and then says to him, 'Go wherever you wish. I have no share in your inheritance, nor am I responsible for any liability on your behalf.' He must have two witnesses testify to this declaration."
